title: Matching objects in SR(X) of a simplicial etale X-scheme are its matching schemes
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme with small etale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and let $U_\bullet\to X$ be an augmented simplicial $X$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover] with simplicial operators $U(\varphi)$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] and with every structure morphism $U_n\to X$ etale. For $n\geq0$ let $M_n(U)$ be its matching scheme: $M_0(U)=X$, and for $n\geq1$ the limit, in schemes over $X$, of the diagram formed by the terms $U_k$, $k<n$, indexed by the injective non-identity order-preserving maps $\delta:[k]\to[n]$, with the simplicial operators between them; let $\mu^U_n:U_n\to M_n(U)$ be the matching map, whose $\delta$-component is $U(\delta)$ (for $n=0$ the augmentation $U_0\to X$). Let $K$ be the simplicial object of the category $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ of semi-representable objects over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object] with $K_n$ the one-member family $\{U_n\to X\}$ and $K(\varphi)=(\mathrm{id},(U(\varphi)))$. Then for every $n\geq0$: (1) $M_n(U)$ exists and $M_n(U)\to X$ is etale, so $M_n(U)$ is an object of $X_{\Et}$; (2) there is an isomorphism in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ from the matching object $M_n(K)$ of [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object] to the one-member family $\{M_n(U)\to X\}$ under which the matching morphism $K_n\to M_n(K)$ corresponds to the morphism $\{U_n\}\to\{M_n(U)\}$ with component $\mu^U_n$; (3) $K_n\to M_n(K)$ is a covering in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ if and only if $\mu^U_n$ is surjective. Consequently $K$ is a hypercover of $X$ in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ if and only if $\mu^U_n$ is an etale covering (a surjective etale morphism) for every $n\geq0$.

proof.text: (Finite limits in $X_{\Et}$ and in schemes over $X$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (2), applied to $V=X$, the category $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] has the final object $\mathrm{id}_X$, and for morphisms $W_1\to W\leftarrow W_2$ of $X_{\Et}$ the scheme-theoretic fibre product $W_1\times_WW_2$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with its map to $X$, is etale over $X$ and a fibre product in $X_{\Et}$; hence $X_{\Et}$ has finite limits by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-limits-from-terminal-pullbacks] (1). Let $\mathrm{Sch}/X$ be the category of schemes over $X$ with $X$-morphisms, and $j:X_{\Et}\to\mathrm{Sch}/X$ the inclusion (the morphisms of $X_{\Et}$ are all $X$-morphisms). $j$ carries final objects to final objects: a final object of $X_{\Et}$ is isomorphic to $\mathrm{id}_X$, and $\mathrm{id}_X$ is final in $\mathrm{Sch}/X$ (the only $X$-morphism $T\to X$ is the structure morphism). $j$ carries fibre product squares to fibre product squares: a fibre product square in $X_{\Et}$ is isomorphic to the one of $W_1\times_WW_2$, and $W_1\times_WW_2$ is a fibre product in $\mathrm{Sch}/X$, because for an $X$-scheme $T$ a pair of morphisms $T\to W_1$, $T\to W_2$ agreeing in $W$ consists of $X$-morphisms as soon as one of them is one, and the induced $T\to W_1\times_WW_2$ is then an $X$-morphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-limits-from-terminal-pullbacks] (2), $j$ preserves finite limits. Finally every $U_n$ is an object of $X_{\Et}$ and every $U(\varphi)$ an $X$-morphism, so $U$ is also a simplicial object $U^{\mathrm{et}}$ of $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], with $j\circ U^{\mathrm{et}}=U$.

proof.text: (Part (1) and the matching map.) For $n=0$, $M_0(U)=X$ with $\mathrm{id}_X$, which is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1) (an identity is an open immersion), and $\mu^U_0$ is the augmentation. Let $n\geq1$. By step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-matching-object] (1),(3) for $\mathcal C=X_{\Et}$, the matching object $M'_n=M_n(U^{\mathrm{et}})$ of $X_{\Et}$ with projections $\mathrm{pr}_i$ and matching morphism $\mu'_n$ exists. By [lem-weil-pbc-matching-object-proper-faces] (2),(3) for $\mathcal C=X_{\Et}$, $(M'_n,(\pi_\delta)_\delta)$ is a limit cone of the diagram $P_n(U^{\mathrm{et}})$ indexed by the injective order-preserving $\delta:[k]\to[n]$ with $k<n$ (these are exactly the injective non-identity ones), and $\pi_\delta\circ\mu'_n=U(\delta)$. The diagram $j\circ P_n(U^{\mathrm{et}})$ is the diagram in $\mathrm{Sch}/X$ defining $M_n(U)$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover]; since $j$ preserves finite limits (step 1) and $\mathcal I_n$ is finite, $(M'_n,(\pi_\delta))$ is a limit of it in $\mathrm{Sch}/X$. So $M_n(U)$ exists, and (limits being unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with the projections) we may take $M_n(U)=M'_n$ with the projections $\pi_\delta$; its structure morphism to $X$ is etale since $M'_n$ is an object of $X_{\Et}$. This is (1). The matching map $\mu^U_n$ is the unique $X$-morphism with $\delta$-components $U(\delta)$; since $\pi_\delta\circ\mu'_n=U(\delta)$, $\mu^U_n=\mu'_n$.

proof.text: (One-member families are closed under finite limits.) Let $\iota:X_{\Et}\to\mathrm{SR}(X)$ be the functor $T\mapsto\{T\}$, $h\mapsto(\mathrm{id},(h))$ of [def-weil-pbc-formal-coproduct] (with $\mathrm{SR}(X)=\mathrm{SR}(X_{\Et})$ by [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object] (1)). By [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits] (1) for $\mathcal C=X_{\Et}$, $\iota(\mathrm{id}_X)=\{\mathrm{id}_X\}$ is final in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$; as every final object of $X_{\Et}$ is isomorphic to $\mathrm{id}_X$, $\iota$ carries final objects to final objects. For morphisms $A\to S\leftarrow B$ of $X_{\Et}$, [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits] (2) with one-point index sets $I=J=K$ says that the one-member family $\{A\times_SB\}$ (indexed by the single pair) with the projections $(\mathrm{id},(p_1))=\iota(p_1)$, $(\mathrm{id},(p_2))=\iota(p_2)$ is a fibre product of $\iota(A)\to\iota(S)\leftarrow\iota(B)$ in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$; since fibre products are unique up to isomorphism, $\iota$ carries every fibre product square of $X_{\Et}$ to a fibre product square. By step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-limits-from-terminal-pullbacks] (2), $\iota$ preserves finite limits.

proof.text: (Part (2).) By its definition $K=\iota\circ U^{\mathrm{et}}$. For $n=0$, $M_0(K)=\{\mathrm{id}_X\}=\{M_0(U)\}$ and $\mu_0$ is the unique morphism $\{U_0\}\to\{\mathrm{id}_X\}$, namely $(\mathrm{id},(U_0\to X))=\iota(\mu^U_0)$. Let $n\geq1$. The diagram $D_n(K)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-matching-object] defining $M_n(K)$ [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object] (4) is $\iota\circ D_n(U^{\mathrm{et}})$ (same index category, objects $\{U_{n-1}\}$, $\{U_{n-2}\}$, arrows $\iota(d_i)$). By step 3, $(\{M'_n\},(\iota(\mathrm{pr}_i))_i)$ is a limit of $D_n(K)$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-matching-object] (1) there is a unique isomorphism $\psi:M_n(K)\to\{M'_n\}=\{M_n(U)\}$ with $\iota(\mathrm{pr}_i)\circ\psi=\mathrm{pr}^K_i$ for all $i$. Both $\psi\circ\mu_n$ and $\iota(\mu'_n)$ are morphisms $K_n\to\{M'_n\}$ whose composites with $\iota(\mathrm{pr}_i)$ are $d^K_i=\iota(d_i)$ (as $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ\mu'_n=d_i$); by the bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-matching-object] (2) (for the limit $\{M'_n\}$) they are equal. By step 2, $\iota(\mu'_n)=(\mathrm{id},(\mu^U_n))$. This is (2).

source.place: Lemma 0186 (lemma-formula-limit): the matching object is determined by the functor of compatible tuples of faces

proof.text: (Part (3).) First, an isomorphism $(\beta,(f_i)):\{A_i\}_{i\in I}\to\{B_j\}_{j\in J}$ of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ with inverse $(\beta',(g_j))$ is a covering: the composition rule of [def-weil-pbc-formal-coproduct] gives $\beta'\circ\beta=\mathrm{id}_I$, $\beta\circ\beta'=\mathrm{id}_J$, $g_{\beta(i)}\circ f_i=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{\beta'(j)}\circ g_j=\mathrm{id}$, so for each $j$ the family $\{f_i:\beta(i)=j\}$ is the single isomorphism $f_{\beta'(j)}$, which is surjective and etale (an isomorphism is an open immersion, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1)), hence a covering family of $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]; so it is a covering by [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object] (3). By step 4, $\iota(\mu^U_n)=\psi\circ\mu_n$ and $\mu_n=\psi^{-1}\circ\iota(\mu^U_n)$ with $\psi,\psi^{-1}$ coverings; by [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-covering-permanence] (1), $\mu_n$ is a covering iff $\iota(\mu^U_n)$ is. By [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object] (3), $\iota(\mu^U_n)=(\mathrm{id},(\mu^U_n))$ is a covering iff the one-member family $\{\mu^U_n:U_n\to M_n(U)\}$ is a covering family of $X_{\Et}$, i.e. iff $\mu^U_n$ is etale and surjective [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. As $U_n$ and $M_n(U)$ are etale over $X$ (part (1)) and $\mu^U_n$ is an $X$-morphism, $\mu^U_n$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (3). So $\mu_n$ is a covering iff $\mu^U_n$ is surjective. This is (3).

source.place: Definition 01G3 (definition-covering-SR) of coverings in SR(C, X), for one-member families

proof.text: (Consequence.) By [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object] (5), $K$ is a hypercover of $X$ in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ iff $\mu_n$ is a covering for every $n\geq0$, iff (step 5) $\mu^U_n$ is surjective for every $n$; since every $\mu^U_n$ is etale (step 5), this says that every $\mu^U_n$ is a surjective etale morphism, i.e. an etale covering.

split_report.summary: Proof written in six steps. The comparison of the two descriptions of the matching diagram (all proper faces, as in def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover and lem-weil-pbc-matching-object-fibre-product, against the codimension-1/2 diagram D_n of lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-matching-object) is the new node lem-weil-pbc-matching-object-proper-faces (Stacks 0186 for injective maps). The key fact that the inclusions X_Et -> Sch/X and X_Et -> SR(X) (one-member families) preserve finite limits is derived from preservation of the final object and fibre products (lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits (2), lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits (1),(2) with one-point index sets) through the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-limits-from-terminal-pullbacks (preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesTerminal_and_pullbacks). Part (3) uses that isomorphisms of SR(X) are coverings (written out) and covering-permanence (1), and etaleness of X-morphisms between etale X-schemes. Statement and stmt_deps kept.
